greet.text: Meet Maya, who runs billing at a small spine clinic.

biller.text: Oh, come on! Another MRI, denied? Okay. The clock's ticking.

grind.text: To fight it, Maya has to dig up the payer's policy, read it rule by rule,
match the chart, and write the letter. That's hours. Per denial.
Payers check rule by rule. Why can't Maya?

stakes.text: Here's the wild part. In Medicare Advantage in 2024,
80.7 percent of appealed prior auth denials were overturned.

pitch.text: It checks each denial against the payer's own policy and tells you what to do next,

worklist.text: It starts with the worklist: every denial,
ranked by what to do and when it's due.
Deadlines come from a fixed rules table, never from the model.

case.text: This Medicare Advantage plan denied a lumbar MRI for having no x-ray first.
Nemotron reads the fax, and a reason-code table sends it to clinical review.

rules.text: It pulls the Medicare policy in force on the date of service from the CMS Coverage API,
and matches each rule, in the payer's own words, to the chart.
Nothing here asks for an x-ray first.

appeal.text: So a fixed rule says: appeal.
and the citation gate checks every quote against its source.

tamper.text: Now, change one word. Four weeks becomes two weeks.
The quote turns void, the real sentence appears beside it, and export locks.
A person always sends the letter.

physician.text: When the chart is missing something, it doesn't guess.
It asks the physician, quoting the rule,
to document only care that actually happened.

check.text: Before a request goes out, the same checks run on the prior auth.
Aetna needs six weeks of therapy and the chart shows thirty-eight days,
so code works out the earliest date it qualifies.

how.text: NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory reads the letter and matches the rules,
and Tavily finds Aetna's current policy at runtime.
But code, not the model, decides verdicts, deadlines,
and whether a quote is real.

proof.text: On thirty synthetic cases we wrote ourselves,
it got every recommendation and all 138 rule statuses right,
at about five cents a case.
That's the pipeline working as designed, not accuracy on real charts.

close.text: Denial Auditor checks a denial in minutes and verifies every quote,
so a small practice can see which appeals are worth filing.
Try the live demo at the link on screen.
Denial Auditor, by team Road House. Thanks for watching.
